record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.context_brief: Finite basis decision problem for identical inclusions
record.original_question: Find an algorithm that decides whether the inclusive variety generated by a given finite set of finite semigroups can be defined by a finite system of elementary identical inclusions, or prove that no such algorithm exists.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.10. (G. Mashevitzky) Find an algorithm that decides whether the inclusive variety
generated by a given finite set of finite semigroups, can be defined by a finite system of (elementary)
identical inclusions or prove that such an algorithm does not exist. (This problem is similar to
Tarski’s problem for identities).
          In [11], a finite semigroup was constructed that does not have a finite basis for its ele-
mentary identical inclusions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

Let S be a semigroup. An identical inclusion over S (in the sense of Lyapin) is a universally closed expression of the form
   w(x_1,…,x_n) ∈ {w_1(x_1,…,x_n), w_2(x_1,…,x_n), …, w_k(x_1,…,x_n)},
where w, w_1, …, w_k are semigroup words in the variables x_1,…,x_n. A semigroup S satisfies this identical inclusion if, for every assignment of the variables x_1,…,x_n to elements of S, the value of w equals the value of at least one of the words w_i. An identical inclusion is called elementary if k is finite (only finitely many words appear on the right-hand side).

A class K of semigroups is called an inclusive variety if it is the class of all semigroups satisfying some (possibly infinite) system Σ of identical inclusions. The inclusive variety generated by a set X of semigroups is the smallest inclusive variety containing X, equivalently the class of all semigroups satisfying every identical inclusion that holds in every member of X.

An inclusive variety V is said to be finitely based by elementary identical inclusions if there is a finite system Σ of elementary identical inclusions such that V is exactly the class of all semigroups satisfying Σ.

Problem.

Decide the following question algorithmically: given as input a finite list S_1, S_2, …, S_m of finite semigroups (each presented by its multiplication table), determine whether the inclusive variety generated by {S_1,…,S_m} is finitely based by elementary identical inclusions. Either exhibit such an algorithm, or prove that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as an unsolved entry attributed to G. Mashevitzky in a recently compiled collection of open problems in semigroup theory (Lyapin's notebook). Recent work (e.g., a 2025 Algebra Universalis paper on nonelementary inclusive varieties) continues to study related structural questions but does not announce a decision algorithm or an undecidability proof for this specific finite-basis problem for inclusive varieties of finite semigroups.

status_evidence.title: Nonelementary inclusive varieties of groups and semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies inclusive varieties and identical inclusions in semigroups and groups, but does not resolve the algorithmic finite-basis question for inclusive varieties generated by finite semigroups.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to investigate inclusive varieties without resolving the decision problem.
